## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads.

## Cache saturation
At death_q=0.01, cost FALLS monotonically from 8.469 ns/p (N=10000, past the L1d spill at N≈963) to 7.263 ns/p (N=10000000), with no knee at the L2→DRAM spill at N≈61680 — N=100000 already sits in DRAM at 7.648 ns/p and cost continues to decline. This flat-to-falling shape indicates overhead amortization dominates at small N and the algo is not bandwidth-limited at the spill. Raising the death rate lifts the floor without altering the N-shape: q=0.1 holds ~8.9 ns/p, q=0.25 holds ~11.0, q=0.5 holds ~13.4, all essentially flat across N.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 9.36 GB/s at N=10000000, death_q=0.01 — 31% of the 29.9 GB/s streaming ceiling. The algo is compute/overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound: cost falls rather than rises at the DRAM spill, and compute occupies 60–70% of cycles at low churn. Death rate drives a transition to branch-bound: branch_flush rises from 4.2% (q=0.01, N=1M) to 36.6% (q=0.5, N=1M), and achieved bandwidth falls to 5.11 GB/s (17% of ceiling). The algo never enters a bandwidth-bound regime.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized component-wise within a single particle, not across particles. `fmul.4s v0, v3, v4` and `fadd.4s v0, v1, v0` operate on four floats of one particle's position; `ext.16b v3, v1, v2, #0xc` and `mov.s v3[3], v0[0]` rearrange components into lanes. A gather appears: `ld1.s {v2}[1], [x8]` loads one float into a single lane. The render loop is entirely scalar: `ldrb`/`strb` byte stores (`strb w2, [x1]`, `strb w2, [x1, #0x1]`, `strb w2, [x1, #0x2]`) with `csel` clamping — 18 `csel` and 19 `strb` instructions. The component-wise 4s vectorization on stride-68 particles explains why bandwidth stays at 31% of ceiling; the byte-granular scatter stores and per-particle branching prevent streaming.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo never exceeds 9.36 GB/s (31% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling) at q=0.01, and branch_flush consumes up to 36.8% of cycles at q=0.5, dropping bandwidth to 4.98 GB/s. Component-wise auto-vectorization on stride-68 particles with a scalar byte-scatter render loop cannot approach the streaming ceiling in any regime.
